claims.statement: infrastructure-as-code/ defines each local environment as one of four named Docker Compose stacks (auth, mcm, audit, observability), each its own Compose project whose aggregator file is an include:-only list of that stack's per-service compose files, and each brought up through an Nx target that pins the project name, the aggregator file and the stack's gitignored .env rather than a bare docker compose invocation.

The local stack lifecycle targets encode manual ordering and a complete teardown: up-all runs auth then mcm serially (parallel: false), and each down-* target names every profile that stack might have been brought up with (all five for mcm, vault for auth) so profile-gated containers are actually removed.

Per-service profiles: assignments live inside the included component compose files rather than being re-declared in the stack aggregator, which removes the include-override merge that only newer Docker Compose accepted and lets the stack parse on any conformant Compose.

stacks.toml declares seven deploy=true [[stack]] blocks whose after= edges form the production deploy order: prod-auth is the root, prod-mc-service waits on it, prod-mcm-bff waits on prod-mc-service, prod-movie-assistant waits on prod-mcm-bff, prod-vault waits on prod-auth, prod-observability waits on prod-mcm-bff for ordering only, and prod-audit is an independent root.

Each production stack's environment block is the only declaration of that stack's required inputs: Komodo writes it into the stack's env_file_path (.env.prod), and the three CI-built stacks (prod-mc-service, prod-mcm-bff, prod-movie-assistant) additionally receive their committed host-free .env.deploy as additional_env_files, while the four upstream-image stacks (prod-auth, prod-audit, prod-observability, and prod-vault, which declares an env_file_path but no environment block at all) take none.

scripts/__tests__/komodo-stack-env.guard.test.mjs makes the stacks.toml-to-prod-compose coupling mechanical and one-directional: it requires every ${VAR:?...} in a stack's compose files to be supplied by that stack's environment block or additional_env_files, but it cannot detect an environment key that no compose reads.

A stack environment key can outlive its consumer, and both prod bind-prefix variables have now run that course to completion: prod-auth stopped passing KC_ADMIN_BIND_IP on 2026-10-12 (feature 028 dropped it from the keycloak compose bind), and prod-observability stopped passing TS_ADMIN_IP on 2026-10-13 (feature 028 made the two operator-UI binds 0.0.0.0), so no stack or compose file reads either name and both Komodo Variables can be retired — leaving one seeded only costs dead config, since the admin URL uses the separate KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN.

The committed Komodo config is host-free by construction: the git host lives in a separately bootstrapped Repo resource referenced by name and the domain/tailnet/registry values are masked [[NAME]] Variables, with scripts/check-komodo-sync.mjs failing on a *.ts.net host, a Tailscale CGNAT address or a non-[[var]] URL authority in infrastructure-as-code/komodo/**/*.toml (comments included), and scripts/check-topology-scrub.mjs covering real tailnet hosts elsewhere in the tree.

Image digests are deliberately outside stacks.toml: cd-deploy promotes each built image's immutable digest into a tracked, host-free .env.deploy beside the component compose, which the stack receives as additional_env_files (passed last so the digest interpolates from git), and the compose assembles ${REGISTRY_HOST}/jumbleknot/<svc>@${<SVC>_DIGEST}.

The ResourceSync adopts the four live core production stacks in place rather than creating them, because their Komodo Stack names already match the TOML; a rename is not a plain config diff, since Komodo sets the Compose project name from the Stack name and overrides the compose name: field.

Production admin/UI publishes must sit in the reserved host-port range 19000-19099, enforced by scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs, which compares the fixed host port numbers of every compose.prod.yaml against every other tracked compose file (host_ip ignored) because the prod and CI rootless daemons publish into one shared host port space.

Every long-running service in a compose.prod.yaml must declare restart: always: scripts/check-prod-restart-policy.mjs forbids unless-stopped and a missing policy outright and permits restart: no / on-failure only for one-shot init/seed containers, because the host's graceful-shutdown drain stops containers to Exited(0) and unless-stopped then declines to bring them back when the daemon starts.

prod-vault is deployed deliberately dormant: its prod compose runs a real Vault server (not -dev) with a healthcheck override that reports healthy while uninitialized and sealed, and the stack carries no environment block because a dormant Vault has no root token to inject.

The no-cross-project-depends_on rule between local stacks fails as a working-looking 401 rather than a crash: mc-service serves /health while Keycloak is unreachable and still rejects every protected request, behaviour pinned by unauthenticated_401_is_returned_even_when_keycloak_is_unreachable in backend/mc-service/tests/integration/health_test.rs.

A Compose profile is not isolation from interpolation: Compose interpolates every service in an included file at parse time regardless of which profiles are selected, which is why the backup destination services live in their own compose file brought up explicitly rather than as another mcm profile.

Production publishes exactly three host ports, and all three are operator surfaces bound plainly to 0.0.0.0 on prod-reserved ports rather than to the tailnet IP: prod-observability publishes LangFuse web (19030:3000) and Grafana inside otel-lgtm (19002:3000), and prod-auth publishes the Keycloak admin console (19099:8080). The 0.0.0.0 bind is forced rather than chosen — the rootless daemon starts before tailscaled at boot, so a ${TS_ADMIN_IP}:host:container publish silently fails to bind (rootlesskit never learns the tailnet IP, the container ends up with no ports and nothing listens) — and tailnet-only exposure is preserved instead by the host firewall's default-deny on non-tailnet inbound. Every other service in the production topology is unpublished and reached by internal DNS, including otel-lgtm's OTLP 4317/4318 and OPA's 8181, and all three published ports sit in the prod-reserved 19000-19099 range so they cannot collide with the CI runner's own LangFuse, Grafana or Keycloak on the shared host.

Dev-stack credentials are mostly fail-fast ${VAR:?} interpolation references, but the stacks README enumerates three exception classes: the BFF (bff/compose.yaml) takes its credentials from frontend/mcm-app/.env.docker via a service-local env_file:, web-api-mcp (web-api-mcp/compose.yaml) does the same from mcp-servers/web-api-mcp/.env.local, and the agent gateway keeps deliberately optional ${VAR:-} keys (AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_SECRET, allowlisted by name in scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs, plus the AGENT_GATEWAY_CLIENT_ID/model defaults) so the gateway comes up without token exchange and tool calls fail closed. The real values for the ${VAR:?} references live in gitignored per-stack <stack>.env files minted from committed <stack>.env.example templates by scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs, and the interpolation source is pinned per include rather than blanket: every include of auth/audit/observability carries an env_file: pin to that stack's .env, while mcm pins only the two component files that interpolate a stack-scoped variable (agent-db and agent-gateway, for ${AGENT_DB_PASSWORD}) and includes its other five bare; the same .env is passed again as the Nx up-* target's --env-file.

The local agent layer has two distinct bring-up paths: up-mcm-agents runs scripts/up-mcm-agents.mjs, the heavy in-stack agents-profile variant that fetches the agent-gateway Keycloak client secret and injects it so token-exchange tool calls work, while up-agents-prod runs scripts/agent-stack.mjs, the light containerized production-node stack used for local agent E2E.

infrastructure-as-code/clickhouse/config.d/mcm-system-logs.xml is a non-stack side artifact bind-mounted read-only into langfuse-clickhouse by both the dev and the prod observability compose files: it removes ClickHouse's own system.trace_log and system.text_log tables and gives every other existing system-log table a 3-day TTL, while leaving opentelemetry_span_log at its default because its section defines a full <engine> and ClickHouse refuses a separate <ttl> there and fails to start.

infrastructure-as-code/opa/policies/ is part of the observability stack definition rather than baked into an image: both the dev and prod observability compose files bind-mount it read-only into opa-service, which runs with --watch /policies, and the directory holds the agent_ui_action and agent_token_exchange policies with their _test.rego suites.

infrastructure-as-code/docker/dev-ollama.compose.yaml is a dev-container-only helper that belongs to no stack: it is not part of the production agent stack (which serves via host Ollama) and publishes 0.0.0.0:11434 rather than loopback so a nested agent-gateway container can reach it via host.docker.internal without any gateway/compose change.

The guardrails CI 'naming' job runs the compose static gates over the files it discovers by basename — scripts/check-resource-naming.mjs (enforcing the <context>-<role>-<engine> grammar on declared volume/network/container names, container_name == service key, the BFF-only mcm- qualifier, and no retired service key re-introduced as a network alias) and scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs (requiring every secret-shaped key, password-bearing URL and command/healthcheck/entrypoint auth literal to be a pure ${VAR} or ${VAR:?} reference, and failing an inline ${VAR:-default}) — where discovery is the globs infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose*.yaml plus infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.compose.yaml plus the retired root compose.yaml by name, so a file whose basename does not begin with 'compose' (e.g. infrastructure-as-code/docker/dev-ollama.compose.yaml) escapes all three basename-discovering gates; the infra-scan target separately enumerates and Trivy-scans the third-party images pulled in infrastructure-as-code/**.

scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs is idempotent and back-filling rather than skip-on-exists: on an existing <stack>.env it preserves every value already present (including hand-edited ones) and only seeds keys the template has since gained, so a newly added key never requires --force; a <generate:KIND> key present but empty is minted in place while a blank fixture key is left untouched, deterministic fixtures such as LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_PUBLIC_KEY/SECRET_KEY are copied verbatim even under --force, and a run prints key names only, never values.

The generation kinds are implemented by scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs and include mongo-keyfile (base64 replica-set keyfile content for MONGO_MC_KEYFILE) alongside b62-32, b62-48, hex-64, complex-16, unleash-admin and unleash-client; the stacks README's kind list omits mongo-keyfile even though the mcm template declares it.

No dev-stack template carries a topology value any more: feature 080 removed the deliberately blank REGISTRY_HOST= from both mcm.env.example and observability.env.example when the from-source object-store image became upstream RustFS, and mcm.compose.yaml keeps only the note about the interpolation failure it once caused. The generator rule that remains is that a template key which is not a <generate:KIND> placeholder is never filled, so a blank entry stays blank and a complete <stack>.env still reports 'up to date'; in production REGISTRY_HOST is a per-stack Komodo Variable declared in stacks.toml instead.

The committed-template contract is backed by .gitignore, which ignores *.env and *.env.* and carves out !infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.env.example; the carve-out is scoped to that directory so other deliberately ignored *.env.example files stay ignored.

All seven [[stack]] blocks in stacks.toml name the same Komodo Periphery server (server = "Local"), the same linked_repo = "mcm-repo" and the same branch = "main", so a single ResourceSync reconciles the whole production topology against one host and one repository branch.

The three feature-025 Control-Tower support stacks (prod-audit, prod-observability, prod-vault) are the opposite of the four core stacks on the adopt-versus-create axis: the core stacks already existed as hand-created Komodo Stacks carrying the canonical names and were adopted in place, whereas the support stacks arrive as new [[stack]] blocks with no pre-existing Komodo Stack, so the ResourceSync's first apply of each is a create — a from-scratch deploy. Because the same sync can do either, a new block's diff is previewed so the operation is a known ADOPT-or-CREATE rather than a surprise.

The infra-image CVE scan excludes an image by build ownership — membership of BUILT_IMAGE_NAMES, the six images cd-deploy builds — rather than by registry prefix, so a jumbleknot/-namespaced image cd-deploy does not build is still enumerated and scanned; feature 080 deleted the one from-source object-store image that ever needed the distinction, so upstream rustfs/rustfs is scanned by this keyless sweep like any other third-party image and its name left the exclusion list in the same change, since leaving it would exclude an image nothing scans. The invariant is that every image is scanned by exactly one scanner.

Feature 080 changed prod-observability's declared inputs in both directions: REGISTRY_HOST and LANGFUSE_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD left the stack's environment block because it no longer pulls a ${REGISTRY_HOST}/jumbleknot/… image, and LANGFUSE_RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY was added for the upstream RustFS store (its access key being the literal langfuse, the non-secret public half of the key pair). The Komodo Variables for the two departed names are deliberately kept until the rollback window closes, because reverting the merge restores the lines that need them and a revert cannot recreate a Komodo Variable.

A Komodo Variable referenced by a stack's environment block must be seeded before the sync that first references it: an unseeded [[VAR]] interpolates empty, and the ${VAR:?} guard in that stack's prod compose then aborts the deploy, which is the intended fail-fast rather than a silent default.

scripts/infra-image-scan.mjs refuses to report on a partial image set: it resolves ${REGISTRY_HOST} in an image ref when the variable is set (this project's own images can only be written that way, because check-topology-scrub.mjs forbids the real host in a committed file), and when the variable is unset it exits 2 naming the skipped locations on a real scan while only warning on --list — because a sweep that quietly covers less of the tree and still passes is indistinguishable from one that scanned everything and found nothing.

The compose static gates are self-verified and locally reproducible: the secret gate runs in the naming job as --selftest then scan (so a detector that silently stopped flagging cannot report green), the naming gate has no selftest and is invoked plain as --section=all, and scripts/preflight.mjs reproduces both locally with the same argument shapes.

The tracked digest-by-git promotion files are distributed and kept tracked by name: cd-deploy's ENV_DEPLOY_PATHS names exactly three run directories (infrastructure-as-code/docker/bff, mc-service, agents), the promotion step copies the same generated VAR=<bare sha256> block into each so every Komodo Stack reads a local .env.deploy instead of a relative path, and .gitignore keeps those files tracked via an !infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/.env.deploy carve-out beside the *.env / *.env.* ignore rule because the file carries digests only, no host or secret.

prod-auth's keycloak-network is the one production network that is NOT external: keycloak/compose.prod.yaml declares it as an empty `keycloak-network: {}` map so Compose manages it, deliberately since feature 029, because it carries only the intra-stack keycloak-service to keycloak-store-postgres DB link (the BFF reaches Keycloak over backend-network) and a Compose-managed network is created with both services attached atomically on every up/recreate — so Keycloak can always resolve its Postgres even when the shared external networks hit the rootless re-attach race that stranded keycloak-service in the 2026-07-06 outage. The consequences a reader must know: Compose therefore names it prod-auth_keycloak-network (do not add a `name:` — adopting the old unlabeled external net errors with an incorrect label), and the one-time cutover on a host still carrying the pre-029 external net is `docker network rm keycloak-network` after a prod-auth destroy.

The prod observability compose caps langfuse-clickhouse where the dev file does not — mem_limit: 4g, memswap_limit: 4g (no swap beyond the cap, since Docker's default memswap is 2x mem_limit) and cpus: 2 — because prod observability shares the physical host with the CI runner and on 2026-10-02 this container ran at ~725% CPU with swap full and slowed every CI job 2-3x; the ClickHouse image is cgroup-aware, so the container limit also bounds its internal max_server_memory_usage. The capacity check recorded in the prod control-tower runbook retained that 4g cap deliberately rather than lowering it.

Spec 081 US8b's observability database cutover is an external-resource contract, not just an image bump: both prod volumes are renamed (observability-langfuse-postgres-v18-data, observability-unleash-postgres-v18-data) and declared external: true with the pre-18 `…-postgres-data` volumes left untouched as the rollback, so the operator must create the new volumes — and restore the Unleash dump into its own — BEFORE the merge that deploys the file; a merge that lands first fails on the missing external volume and creates zero containers rather than bringing LangFuse up on an empty store. The asymmetry is deliberate: ADR-0002 §4 ratifies losing the LangFuse trace history, not Unleash's flag state.

In both the dev and the prod observability compose files, langfuse-postgres and unleash-postgres reference one identical digest-pinned Postgres image and both mount the PARENT path /var/lib/postgresql rather than the pre-18 /data path, because postgres 18 keeps its cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker and a mount left on the older path makes the entrypoint exit 1 even on an empty volume. scripts/__tests__/langfuse-postgres-shared-pin.guard.test.mjs pins all three facts together — the shared pin, its presence on the 18 line, and the parent mount — because a find-and-replace image bump would otherwise migrate Unleash's store as a silent side effect of a LangFuse change.

infrastructure-as-code/docker/backups/compose.yaml's two backup destinations are built around two constraints beyond being a separate file: the WebDAV config and htpasswd live in a named volume written by a one-shot rather than a bind mount, because the dev container's Docker is a Sandbox microVM sharing only /workspaces so a bind source outside it (a git worktree under /home/coder) is silently created as an empty directory and the container fails with `is a directory`; and the destination credentials reach curl through the container's environment, referenced as `$$VAR` and fed to `curl -K -` on stdin, never interpolated by Compose into the entrypoint where docker inspect and ps could read them. Both destinations bind 127.0.0.1 only, and the backup URL guard denies loopback by default — the inverse of the Ollama guard — which is why scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs names mcm-bff-backup-rustfs and mcm-bff-backup-webdav in BACKUP_ALLOWED_DESTINATION_HOSTS for dev.

The prod restart-policy gate's scan is limited to the glob infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose.prod.yaml, so a prod-shaped compose outside that glob is unpoliced, and the host-managed composes (Forgejo, Komodo itself, cloudflared, and the host monitoring/object-store services) live outside the repository entirely — their restart: always is host state an operator maintains by hand, and a host rebuild that forgets it reintroduces the reboot failure for those stacks only. The gate runs selftest-then-scan in the naming job of guardrails.yml and locally through scripts/preflight.mjs alongside the other selftest-capable gates.

The gate's one-shot exemption is a safety valve rather than the shape production uses: the one-shot init/seed containers that exist in the prod composes (langfuse-rustfs-init, unleash-seed, agent-audit-init) are themselves restart: always and idle on `sleep infinity` after an idempotent init, deliberately so Komodo's stack health never counts an exited container as unhealthy.

Because `docker stop` does not change a container's restart policy, a retired prod service whose block is deleted from a compose file keeps running and comes back Up on the next boot; taking an orphan out of the policy (`docker update --restart no <container>`) or removing it is a required operator step before a reboot, and the prod runbook records the containers this was done for.

The dev and prod observability compose files pin different OPA images and healthchecks for one shell reason: the dev file uses the distroless openpolicyagent/opa image and declares no healthcheck, while the prod file uses the -debug variant (distroless has no shell; -debug adds busybox so a healthcheck and a Komodo status exist at all) and its healthcheck invokes the opa binary itself (opa eval --fail ... http.send({...}).status_code == 200, exec form) rather than wget, because that busybox ships no wget, curl or nc — the previous wget form failed every run, so the container read unhealthy from ~2026-09-10 (FailingStreak 130247 by 2026-10-03) while OPA was serving fine.

prod-mcm-bff's environment block is the largest in stacks.toml and is where the scheduled-backup switches live: feature 073's production enablement (item #843 follow-up, 2026-10-25) added BACKUP_CREDENTIAL_ENC_KEY, BACKUP_TICK_SECRET and BACKUP_ALLOWED_DESTINATION_HOSTS, and feature 083 added the consent pair BACKUP_CONSENT_CLIENT_ID / BACKUP_CONSENT_CLIENT_SECRET. Until the first three landed none was set, so scheduled backups were off in production — every private destination was refused, no destination secret could be sealed, and the boot log read 'backup scheduler disabled'. The allow-list is an exact host match with no port and is a plain rather than masked Variable because it is LAN topology, and BACKUP_CREDENTIAL_ENC_KEY must never be rotated casually because it orphans every stored destination secret and offline token.

A stack environment key that nothing requires fails open, and the static coupling guard cannot see it: komodo-stack-env.guard.test.mjs only asks whether every ${VAR:?…} in a stack's prod compose has a supplier, so a capability whose keys are optional in the app's env reader has no static check at all — which is how scheduled backups stayed off in production while every gate was green. A [[stack]] edit alone is also insufficient to deliver new values: Komodo writes the environment block into .env.prod, but a sync that changes only the environment does not recreate the container, so the running service keeps the values it started with until the stack is explicitly Redeployed, and the effective values must be read from the host rather than inferred from the TOML.

The three basename-discovering compose gates do not share one scope: scripts/check-no-inline-secrets.mjs and scripts/check-prod-ci-port-collision.mjs glob infrastructure-as-code/docker/**/compose*.yaml plus infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/*.compose.yaml, while scripts/check-resource-naming.mjs globs only the first of those (so the stack aggregators, which declare no container_name, volume name or network of their own, are outside the naming gate); the naming and inline-secret gates each also add the retired root compose.yaml by name. The shared consequence is that a compose file whose basename does not begin with 'compose' falls outside all three, which is why infrastructure-as-code/docker/dev-ollama.compose.yaml is neither name-checked, secret-checked nor port-checked even though the CVE enumerator's wider infrastructure-as-code/**/*.{yaml,yml} glob does see it.

Not every value in stacks.toml is a Variable token: alongside the masked [[NAME]] references the blocks carry a few deliberate non-secret inline literals — the rendered realm file's absolute path (PROD_REALM_FILE), the backup-consent client id (BACKUP_CONSENT_CLIENT_ID), and the admin-URL shape built around the [[TAILNET_HOST]] token — because the scrub rule is about topology and credentials rather than about keeping the block purely symbolic, and the topology gate flags a literal host, CGNAT address or non-[[var]] URL authority, not a literal path or client id.
